Key implementation files: - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts - Defines the options interface with both nested and flat configuration, matching the story schema: - Nested: `story.pattern`, `story.example`, `req.pattern`, `req.example`. - Flat shorthands: `storyPathPattern`, `storyPathExample`, `requirementIdPattern`, `requirementIdExample`. - Default behavior (backward compatibility): - `getDefaultStoryPattern()` → `/^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/`. - `getDefaultStoryExample()` → `"docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md"`. - `getDefaultReqPattern()` → `/^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/`. - `getDefaultReqExample()` → `"REQ-EXAMPLE"`. - Option normalization and resolution: - `normalizeUserOptions(rawOptions)` handles the single-options-object convention. - `resolvePattern(nestedPattern, nestedFieldName, flatPattern, flatFieldName, defaultPattern)`: - Prefers `nestedPattern` over `flatPattern` when both are provided. - Wraps `new RegExp(effective.value)` in try/catch. - On `RegExp` construction failure, appends a stable diagnostic to the global `optionErrors` array using `buildInvalidRegexError(field, pattern)` and **returns `defaultPattern`**, fulfilling REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT. - `resolveExample(nestedExample, flatExample, defaultExample)`: - Uses nested example if present and non-blank, otherwise flat, otherwise default; implements REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES and REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT. - `resolveOptions(rawOptions)`: - Resets `optionErrors = []`. - Extracts nested and flat fields for `story` and `req`. - Calls `resolvePattern` and `resolveExample` for both story and req. - Populates `resolvedDefaults` (used as a shared fallback) and returns a `ResolvedAnnotationOptions` instance with: - `storyPattern`, `storyExample`, `reqPattern`, `reqExample`. - This provides configurable patterns while defaulting cleanly when options are absent or invalid. - Schema: - `getRuleSchema()` returns a JSON schema array with a single `object` describing: - Nested `story` and `req` objects with `pattern` and `example` of `type: "string"`. - Flat `storyPathPattern`, `storyPathExample`, `requirementIdPattern`, `requirementIdExample` also as `string`. - `additionalProperties: false` to enforce option correctness. - This satisfies REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION and mirrors ESLint best-practice rule schemas.
- src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Imports option helpers: - `{ getResolvedDefaults, resolveOptions, type ResolvedAnnotationOptions, getRuleSchema, getOptionErrors }`. - Uses options in rule metadata: - `meta.schema: getRuleSchema()` wires the JSON schema into ESLint, enforcing configuration structure. - Adds `messages.invalidRuleConfiguration` for configuration errors: - Message: `"Invalid configuration for valid-annotation-format: {{details}}"`. - JSDoc ties this directly to Story 010.1 and `REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION` / `REQ-BACKWARD-COMP`. - Rule behavior (`create` function): - `const options = resolveOptions(context.options || []);` resolves user options into runtime regexes and examples. - `const optionErrors = getOptionErrors();` reads any configuration errors accumulated by `resolvePattern`. - In the `Program` visitor: - If `optionErrors && optionErrors.length > 0`, iterates them and calls `context.report({ node, messageId: "invalidRuleConfiguration", data: { details } })` for each. - Then fetches all comments and passes `options` into `processComment`, so validation always runs using either custom or default patterns. - This arrangement surfaces regex config problems but **continues validation** using safe defaults, matching REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMP. - Story-path validation (`validateStoryAnnotation`): - Uses `options.storyPattern` and `collapseAnnotationValue` to validate `@story` values. - On missing or invalid values, builds error details via `buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options)`, which makes use of the **configured `storyExample`** when present. - If a safe suffix auto-fix is available (`getFixedStoryPath(collapsed)` and it matches `options.storyPattern`), it calls `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix`, which in turn uses `getResolvedDefaults()` to preserve the effective examples and patterns after resolution. - Requirement-ID validation (`validateReqAnnotation`): - Uses `options.reqPattern` and `buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options)`, which incorporates `reqExample` from configuration. - These functions are documented with Story 010.1 tags and requirements for regex validation, backward compatibility, and example-driven messages.
- src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts - `buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options)`: - Uses `options.storyExample` (falling back to `STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH`) to construct clear error messages like: - `Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like "".` - `Invalid story path "" for @story annotation. Expected a path like "".` - `buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options)`: - Uses `options.reqExample` (falling back to `getDefaultReqExample()`) for analogous requirement ID messages. - This wiring proves that custom `storyPathExample` / `requirementIdExample` values directly influence error messages, satisfying REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES.
- src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Existing rule for `@story` path existence and security validation: - Default directories: `const defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"];`. - Configurable via `storyDirectories` in its JSON schema. - The new `valid-annotation-format` options are independent and do not alter this behavior; they allow customizing the **format** of story paths, which can be aligned with any `storyDirectories` configuration by user choice. - There is no conflicting configuration and both rules operate on compatible path structures by default (both centered on `docs/stories/...`). This meets the “works seamlessly” integration criterion in practice.

Core functionality & custom patterns (REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG): - Valid tests showing nested configuration: - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY] custom storyPathPattern accepts alternate extension`: - Code: `// @story stories/feature-010.1-CUSTOM.story.mdx`. - Options: `{ story: { pattern: "^stories\\/[^\\s]+\\.story\\.mdx$", example: "stories/example-010.1-CUSTOM.story.mdx" } }`. - This confirms `story.pattern` controls the story path pattern and the rule accepts matches. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ] custom requirementIdPattern accepts PROJECT-123 style IDs`: - Code: `// @req PROJECT-123`. - Options: `{ req: { pattern: "^[A-Z]+-[0-9]+$", example: "PROJECT-123" } }`. - Confirms `req.pattern` is used to validate requirement IDs. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH] custom patterns accept alternative story and req shapes` combines both nested configs. - Valid tests showing **flat shorthand** configuration: - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY-FLAT]` and `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ-FLAT]` using `storyPathPattern`, `storyPathExample`, `requirementIdPattern`, `requirementIdExample` directly on the options object. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH-FLAT]` validates using both flat story and req options simultaneously. - These confirm that both nested and flat configuration modes work and that flat shorthand maps correctly onto the nested structure.
Regex validation & fallback (REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT): - Nested invalid patterns: - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid storyPathPattern falls back to default behavior`: - Options: `{ story: { pattern: "[unclosed" } }`. - Expects two errors: 1. `invalidRuleConfiguration` with details `Invalid regular expression for option "story.pattern": "[unclosed"`. 2. `invalidStoryFormat` with details showing **default** example `"docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md"`, demonstrating fallback to defaults. - Also expects an auto-fix from `...story` to `...story.md`, confirming that normal behavior and safe auto-fix continue to function under invalid configuration. - Similar pattern for req: invalid `req.pattern: "(unclosed"` reports `invalidRuleConfiguration` and an `invalidReqFormat` error using the default `REQ-EXAMPLE` example. - Flat invalid patterns: - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] invalid flat storyPathPattern falls back to default and reports config error`: - Options: `{ storyPathPattern: "[unclosed" }`. - Expects `invalidRuleConfiguration` with details referencing `storyPathPattern`, plus standard invalidStoryFormat based on default patterns and examples. - `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] invalid flat requirementIdPattern falls back to default and reports config error` similarly validates requirement ID patterns. - These tests prove that all pattern options (nested and flat) are validated as regular expressions, with configuration errors both **reported** and **non-breaking** (fallback to defaults), satisfying REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT.
